_meta.purpose: UNCONTAMINATED held-out set. issue_boundary_gold.jsonl was used to debug toc_solver.py's contents parser (three parser bugs were found and fixed against it), so its numbers are optimistic. This file was drawn afterwards, from domains disjoint from BOTH the running-head rule development and the v1 gold, and the solver was not modified after it was scored.
_meta.sampling: uniform random over `doc_type: issue_compilation` sidecars, one file per domain, excluding every domain in v1's hold_out_of list plus every domain appearing in v1. File size > 400kB. seed 777.
_meta.method: every page of every file was read (first 2 lines, extracted with PyMuPDF) and openings marked before any solver output was inspected.
known_gaps: two of the six files drawn (digitalcommons.pepperdine.edu, www.nslj.org) were not labelled and are omitted -- they were dropped for session length, not for any property of the files, which is a non-random omission
4 issues is far too small to certify a precision bar; it detects gross failure, nothing finer

notes: one article, 'Is Unpublished Unequal?', Cornell Law Review. Constant running head throughout; no contents listing.
one piece, 'Statutes of Limitation', Duquesne Law Review 24:4, printed pp. 975-1126. Scanned/OCR text; head alternates verso/recto.
